whatFailed: The expiry chooser in the Create API token dialog cannot be reached by its visible label because the Radix select trigger has no accessible name: the visible "Expires in" label's htmlFor points at an id that never lands on any DOM element, so getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Expires in' }) matched 0 elements and the step never opened the list.

docClaim.quote: Select an expiration period: never expires, 7 days, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year
docClaim.section: Create an API Token > Generate a new token

observed: Steps 1 to 6 passed: sign-in, /t/guard-owner/settings/tokens, and the Create API token dialog all rendered, and the dialog's Name textbox was found by role+name. Step 7 timed out after 10.1s trying to click combobox "Expires in". The harness inventory line reports exactly one combobox on the page whose inner text is "3 months" (roleInventory in packages/guard-runner/src/web/executor.ts uses allInnerTexts, so that line is visible text, not an accessible name), and step-7.png shows the closed trigger reading "3 months" under a visible "Expires in" label with the dropdown never opened. The dialog's own DOM text at step 6 already lists the six items as "7 days, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 12 months, Never", so the doc's six periods are all present but the last is labelled "12 months", not "1 year".
impact: Accessibility: the expiry chooser is an unnamed form control, so a screen reader announces only its role and current value ("3 months") with no indication of what it selects, and clicking the "Expires in" text does not focus or open it; the same FormControl-wrapping-Select pattern appears 46 times across the app, and only 1 of 84 SelectTriggers carries an aria-label.

rootCause.explanation: FormControl (packages/ui/primitives/form/form.tsx lines 96-111) is a Radix Slot that applies id={formItemId}, aria-describedby and aria-invalid to its single child, and FormLabel (lines 78-95) renders <label htmlFor={formItemId}>. In this field the Slot's child is <Select>, which is SelectPrimitive.Root (packages/ui/primitives/select.tsx line 10), a non-DOM provider component that does not spread unknown props onto the trigger, so the id is dropped and the label's htmlFor dangles. SelectTrigger (select.tsx lines 16-46) forwards no aria-label or aria-labelledby, and the Radix trigger renders a <button role="combobox">; combobox is not a name-from-content role, so the value text "3 months" does not name it either (the scenario note records the same result from an earlier probe run). Net effect: the control has no accessible name at all. The contrast is inside the same dialog: the Name field's FormControl child is <Input>, a real DOM element, so the Slot's id lands, the label associates, and step 6 found textbox "Name" without trouble.

colleagueFinding.note: Agrees that the API-token expiry selector has no accessible name and that the pattern is app-wide, and I found no upstream report, matching their "unreported" claim. Refinements: (a) the exact mechanism is FormControl's Radix Slot handing id to SelectPrimitive.Root, a non-DOM component, so the label's htmlFor dangles, plus role=combobox blocking name-from-content, and the Name field in the same dialog proves the Slot works when the child is a real DOM element; (b) blame is not PR #3076 alone, that PR inherited the nesting from b9e5905469 (2024-02-20); (c) quantified as 46 FormControl-wrapping-Select sites and 1 aria-label across 84 SelectTriggers in the tested tree; (d) their finding does not mention that the harness's "the combobox elements on the page are: 3 months" line is inner text, not an accessible name, which is what makes the control unreachable by any role+name locator.

notes: Two separate things sit behind this one red. First, the reported failure is a markup/accessibility defect, not a violation of the bound doc sentence: the scenario never got to evaluate the six options. Second, and unobserved because step 7 could not act, the doc claim itself is not literally satisfied: EXPIRATION_DATES in token-create-dialog.tsx line 46 labels the longest period "12 months" while the doc enumerates "1 year". The durations are identical (the key ONE_YEAR resolves through packages/lib/constants/time.ts line 11, Duration.fromObject({ years: 1 }), in packages/lib/server-only/public-api/create-api-token.ts), so this is a wording mismatch, not a functional one, and the fix belongs in whichever side the maintainers prefer: the doc at apps/docs/content/docs/developers/getting-started/authentication.mdx or the UI label. The docs live in this same repo under apps/docs/. Minimal code fix for the accessible name: move FormControl to wrap SelectTrigger instead of Select (the shadcn convention), or add aria-label to the SelectTrigger; the same one-line change applied to the shared pattern would fix the other 45 sites.
